summary:
# NOTES: *A Man Made of Money* (Douglas Jerrold, 1849, Punch Office; illustrated by John Leech). Single book; chapters I–XXIV, plus footnote on bees.

## Principal characters
- **Solomon Jericho**: "City Gentleman," ~40 at marriage, dull, matter-of-fact, thin/shrinking. Believed rich via platina mines (lie he told). Becomes "Man made of Money" after wishing aloud "I WISH TO HEAVEN I WAS MADE OF MONEY!" (Ch II); Mrs. Jericho answers "I wish to Heaven you were." Bank-notes emerge from his heart; he shrinks with each note drawn (measured with silk lace around chest). Wears bank paper "skin."
- **Sabilla (Mrs. Jericho)**, widow of Major/Captain Pennibacker (East India, killed by bullet, "Indian tomb"). Repeats "When can you let me have some money?" Imperious, imaginative, snobbish. Calls husband "Solomon."
- **Pennibacker children**: **Basil** (son, ~12 at wedding with gold hunting-watch; later lawyer/student in chambers; "loyalty" = money jargon; "straps" theory; pet terrier Scrub; comic). **Monica** (elder daughter; "Nic"). **Agatha** ("Aggy"; younger, flirtatious, hates "Aggy").
- **Bessy Carraways**: daughter of Gilbert Carraways; goodness, golden hair, silver bee brooch-prize; loved by Basil.
- **Gilbert Carraways**: Squire of Marigolds, merchant, ~60, of Jogtrot Hall; ruined; wife **Mrs. Carraways** ("old butterfly"); later Primrose Place lodgings; emigrates on ship *Halcyon* (Capt. Goodbody) to Antipodes.
- **Hon. Cesar Candituft** ("Man-Tamer," philanthropist, flatterer, "brotherhood of man"); sister **Hon. Miss Caroline Candituft** (tall, cold, pale, amber ringlets; "Minerva"; bridesmaid, marries Sir Arthur).
- **Sir Arthur Hodmadod**, Bart., fool; "when I say X I mean Y" tic; loves Agatha; takes poisoned double dose of physic (Dr. Stubbs' prescription; morphine/hyoscyamus/digitalis) and sleeps through wedding; later marries Miss Candituft.
- **Colonel Bones** (pauper-claimant, "Humph?" tic, "Ugh!"); **Commissioner Thrush** (ex-Siam, "king of Siam" anecdotes, treacle and caterpillars); **Dr. Mizzlemist** (Doctors' Commons, pock-marked, pink nose); **Dr. Stubbs** (physician, prescriber); **Dr. Dodo** (physician, "saw sunlight through hole in Jericho's heart," ruined, emigrates with 9 children, wife Charlotte).
- **Breeks** (tailor) and wife **Julia**; **Bob Topps** (cabman, ex-servant of Carraways) and wife **Jenny** (Jenny White, schoolmaster's daughter, silver bee); **Schoolmaster White** (Goodman White); **Widow Blanket** (school-dame); **Atkins** (valet); **Edwin** (page); **Susan** (servant); **Miss Barnes** (sempstress); **Plutus** (old pauper-servant in garret); tradesmen **Israel, Laban, Issachar**; **Duke of St. George** (debt-ridden; Red Dragon House; Lord Bezant); **Lady Malypense** (duke's daughter); **Doctor Cummin** (St. Shekels church); **Wyse** (maid).
- Fleas (Ch II): elder and younger flea, Æsop lineage, dream-narrators; Jericho's dream (heart plucked by imp, made into paper, gold sovereign army in Bank cellars).

## Chronology
1. Ch I: Mrs. Jericho asks money; Jericho escapes to shave, dresses for dinner at Apollo Tavern. Backstory: widow married Jericho for children; wedding at St. George's ~8 yrs earlier; "You are their father now."
2. Ch II: Jericho returns drunk at dawn; quarrel in bed; "I wish to Heaven I was made of money!" Fleas' dream.
3. Ch III: Mrs. Jericho asks for soda-water/tea; Basil scene (loyalty, "straps," flowers Bessy Carraways vs silk flowers; Carraways invitation to Jogtrot Lodge).
4. Ch IV: Jogtrot Lodge invitation; Mrs. Jericho demands £100; Jericho produces virgin Bank note from heart; "Solomon Jericho was... a Man of Money."
5. Ch V: Jogtrot Hall described; Carraways' benevolence; peacocks; Candituft, Hodmadod ("child of nature," Jenny White as bee); Jericho party arrives in sky-blue phaeton.
6. Ch VI: Garden party; Thrush, Bones, Doctor Mizzlemist; fork pins Jericho's hand ("It's nothing"); Carraways says he's "ruined" later.
7. Ch VII: Breeks measures Jericho (six inches less); Hodmadod plasters Agatha's hand; Candituft/Miss Candituft ploy.
8. Ch VIII: Candituft offers Toadsham seat for £10,000; diamonds and pearls bought (£1,000 paid, Jericho shrinks an inch); Basil reports Carraways ruined; Basil leaves with pearls (Monica & Agatha) in pocket.
9. Ch IX: Jericho MP for Toadsham; Mrs. Jericho's household; Jogtrot Hall visited; Dame Blanket; Bessy's room key.
10. Ch X: Jericho buys Jogtrot Hall (£30,000); apple-tree shower; Basil's apple "maggot at the heart"; Jericho bans Basil; Topps & Jenny; Basil at Silver Lion; Mizzlemist; Jericho insults Bones "toad-eater... bone-picking pauper"; Bones: "I'll have his blood."
11. Ch XI: Carraways ruined, in Primrose Row/Place; Bessy; Basil comes to door; heartsease; "coalheaver" line.
12. Ch XII: Duel: Thrush & Bones challenge Jericho (letter); Candituft ("Cain in high life") forces him; Battersea Fields 8 am; Bones shoots through heart; ball flattened by bank-note wadding; Dr. Dodo testifies.
13. Ch XIII: Dodo's reputation ruined; Stubbs/Mizzlemist; Bob's tale at Horse and Anchor; Breeks; Carraways & Jenny; Candituft receives diamond ring; Basil confronts Candituft.
14. Ch XIV: Jericho's rule; gifts; Basil confronts Jericho with perforated note; Jericho's confession; Mrs. Jericho keeps notes.
15. Ch XV: Basil's 21st birthday; breakfast/pillory vision; Carraways refuses Basil ("Bessy is already provided for"—ship).
16. Ch XVI: Birthday party at Jericho House; Monica proposed to by Candituft; Jericho's dowry refusal; Jericho's fit ("you are... like a devil").
17. Ch XVII: Carraways renounces claim on Jericho; Basil's plan (ploughs, "Lavender"); Mrs. Jericho's visit to Carraways Primrose Place; Basil & mother.
18. Ch XVIII: wedding preparations; Mrs. Jericho visits Mrs. Carraways (white satin); Basil's emigration.
19. Ch XIX: Jericho lends £45,000 to Duke; Hodmadod's double dose; wedding morning: Hodmadod asleep; Agatha left at altar; Candituft (ends engagement later).
20. Ch XX: Hodmadod wakes; Candituft explains; Hodmadod marries Miss Candituft; Jericho turns miser; "two millions of fighting men."
21. Ch XXI: *Halcyon* at docks; Carraways, Basil, Bessy, Mrs. Carraways; Dodo family; Jenny & Bob stow away; "dogmatism is puppyism come to its full growth."
22. Ch XXII: Jericho in garret with Plutus; dealers Israel, Laban, Issachar; councillors meet with Mrs. Jericho; Jericho seizes jewels with poker.
23. Ch XXIII: Basil & Bessy marry at St. Asphodel; bees (Jogtrot swarm) and rooks shipped; Candituft's letter releases Monica; Agatha's comment on Hodmadod.
24. Ch XXIV: Jericho burns the last note in garret; dies a "thin, black paper ash"; all possessions turn to ashes; diamonds to charcoal. Ship sails; Basil & Bessy rejoin; "THE END."

## Key quotes
- "Mr. Jericho, when can you let me have some money?"
- "Woman!" / "Damn Pennibacker!"
- "I WISH TO HEAVEN I WAS MADE OF MONEY!" / "I wish to Heaven you were."
- "Neither you nor any man in this world shall make a cat's-paw of me."
- "Money cannot bestow happiness" (Mrs. J) / "it often supplies a good imitation of the article" (Carraways).
- "Knowledge, turned into ready money, is power" (Bacon, as Jericho cites).
- "Sixteen pounds, thirteen and fourpence a piece."
- "It's nothing." (fork)
- "A duellist is only Cain in higher life."
- "When a heart is wholly made of money, how can it long feel the worst of wounds?"
- "Mr. Jericho, you are not a mother."

## Places
London: Apollo Tavern; St. George's Church (wedding); Bank of England (printing-office, cellars); Ludgate Hill, Cheapside, Bow-Church; Primrose Place/Row; St. Asphodel's; St. Shekels; Red Dragon House; Battersea Fields; Horse and Anchor; Silver Lion (halfway house); Cutancome Club; Doctors' Commons; Primrose Place; Blackwall (docks); Royal Exchange; Rotten Row; Zebra Park. Country: Marigolds village; Jogtrot Hall/Lodge (peacocks, elms, rooks); Toadsham (borough); Wimbledon; Margate; India House; India Docks.

## Numbers
- Jericho's bank: £100 initial; £1,000 for jewels; £15,000 won at play; £30,000 Hall; £45,000 loan to Duke; £10,000 Toadsham seat; £50 (a fortnight earlier).
- Basil's allowance: £100/year (Basil says "a hundred a year").
- Ages: Basil 12 at wedding (8 yrs earlier), 21 at birthday; Jericho 40 at marriage.
